_help: Lists every sprite sheet the game can use. See docs/ART_GUIDE.md. Each sheet is a PNG (path relative to this folder) where every frame is frameWidth x frameHeight pixels, each ROW is one animation, and frames go left to right. 'animations' says which row holds which animation; a sheet can override it (like the egg below). If a sheet is missing an animation, the game uses 'idle' instead. Sheet names here are what src/data/characters.json points at. 'shape' (on pet sheets) names a body shape from 'shapes'. Characters with the same body share a shape, so hats are set up once per shape. A shape's 'head' is where a hat sits: the pixel in the first idle frame where the bottom middle of the hat goes, and 'width': how many pixels wide a hat may be there (the room between ears or horns, or the whole head). The game uses the widest hat size that fits. A shape's 'hats' can nudge one hat on that shape, e.g. { "hat-party": { "x": 1, "y": 2, "width": 10 } }: pixels right and down, and a different width to pick that hat's size. Hat sheets have one frame per size, smallest on the left; the game measures how wide each drawing is. If the automatic hat tracking is off for an animation, a sheet (or a whole shape) can list 'headOffsets', e.g. { "happy": [0, -3, -4, -2] }: how many pixels the head is above (negative) or below the first idle frame, per frame. 'idleSets' are extra idle moves (a stretch, a look around...) that a pet plays now and then instead of its plain idle. Each set lists its moves like 'animations' does, on rows after the usual ones; a sheet that has them drawn on those rows uses the set with 'idleSet'. Hats follow these moves too, sideways as well. A set (or a shape, or a sheet) can fix the sideways tracking with 'headShifts', e.g. { "idle-look": [-1, -2, -2, -1] }: how many pixels the head is right (positive) or left (negative) of the first idle frame, per frame.
